# Causal Chain: From MCP Protocol Design to Agentic Misuse — Which Protocol Features Enable GTG-1002 Class Attacks?

**Problem:** The MCP protocol enabled GTG-1002 by allowing arbitrary tool execution. Understanding which specific protocol design choices created this attack surface supports governance-level protocol hardening.

**Direction:** Analyze MCP protocol specification for: (a) authentication requirements, (b) tool permission scoping, (c) audit logging provisions, (d) rate limiting, (e) scope restriction. For each GTG-1002 attack phase (reconnaissance, exploitation, etc.), identify which MCP feature enabled it. Propose protocol-level mitigations per phase.

**Why it matters:** Protocol-level governance interventions may be more effective than model-level training for agentic misuse. MCP is becoming a standard; governance interventions now can prevent future HACCA-class attacks.

**Relevant context:** GTG-1002 MCP exploitation; Anthropic MCP open standard; HACCA agentic attack analysis.
